This integration connects Viessmann boilers (gas, oil) and heat pumps linked
to the **ViCare** app to Gladys, through the Viessmann cloud: heating, domestic
hot water, temperatures and consumption.

## Requirements

- A Viessmann appliance visible in the ViCare app (Vitoconnect gateway or
  built-in gateway).
- Your ViCare account (e-mail address and password).
- Gladys 5.1 or later, with Internet access.

## 1. Create a client on the Viessmann developer portal

The ViCare API needs a free, personal "client", created once:

1. Open the [Viessmann developer portal](https://app.developer.viessmann-climatesolutions.com)
   and sign in with your ViCare credentials.
2. Create a new client (**Clients** menu).
3. Give it a name (for example "Gladys") and set its **redirect URI** to the
   address shown in the Configuration screen of the integration, under the
   **Connect** button: `https://my.gladysassistant.com/redirect/oauth`. It must
   match character for character. Leave the other options to their defaults.
4. Save, then copy the **Client ID**. No secret is needed.

The free plan ("Basic") is enough: it allows 1450 API calls a day.

## 2. Configure the integration in Gladys

1. In the **Configuration** tab of the integration, paste the client ID and
   **save the configuration**.
2. Only then, in the **ViCare account** block, click **Connect**, sign in with
   your ViCare account and accept the access. Connect uses the saved client
   ID, not the one being typed: clicking it before saving fails.
3. The status turns to "Connected". The **Test the connection** button lists
   the installations, gateways and appliances found.
4. In the **Discovery** tab, add the devices and put each heating circuit in
   its room.

## Devices

For each boiler or heat pump, the integration offers up to three kinds of
devices. Only the features your model actually reports are created.

### One thermostat per heating circuit

| Feature            | Description                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Target temperature | Temperature of the program currently running (normal, reduced, comfort...). Changing it changes that program, like the ViCare app does. |
| Mode               | Off, heating, cooling or auto (see the table below).                                                                                    |
| Operating state    | Idle, heating or cooling, from the burner or compressor.                                                                                |
| Room temperature   | When a room sensor is wired to the circuit.                                                                                             |
| Supply temperature | Temperature of the water sent into the circuit.                                                                                         |

### Domestic hot water (water heater)

| Feature                      | Description                                                     |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hot water target temperature | Requested hot water temperature.                                |
| Hot water mode               | On recent (E3) appliances and heat pumps (see the table below). |
| One-time charge              | Heat the tank once, right now.                                  |
| Hot water heating            | The tank is being heated.                                       |
| Hot water tank temperature   | Temperature measured in the tank.                               |

### Heat generator (boiler or heat pump)

Read-only sensors: outside, boiler, supply and return temperatures (primary
and secondary circuits on heat pumps), burner and compressor (running, number
of starts, operating hours), today's gas consumption (m³ or kWh depending on
the model) and power consumption (kWh).

### Mode mapping

Heating circuit mode:

| ViCare mode                                                 | Gladys mode |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `standby`, `dhw` (hot water only)                           | Off         |
| `heating`, `dhwAndHeating`, `forcedNormal`, `forcedReduced` | Heating     |
| `cooling`                                                   | Cooling     |
| `heatingCooling`, `dhwAndHeatingCooling`                    | Auto        |

Turning a circuit **off** from Gladys picks `dhw` when the appliance supports
it: heating stops but hot water keeps being produced. Hot water has its own
controls, on the water heater device.

Hot water mode:

| ViCare mode                                   | Gladys mode |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `off`                                         | Off         |
| `eco`, `efficient`, `efficientWithMinComfort` | Eco         |
| `balanced`                                    | Auto        |
| `comfort`                                     | Manual      |

**Eco** gathers the economy modes of ViCare (`eco`, `efficient`,
`efficientWithMinComfort`, named "Eco" or "Efficient" in the app depending on
the model). Gladys has no "Comfort" mode for water heaters: ViCare `comfort`
shows as **Manual**.

A mode your appliance does not offer is refused, with a message listing the
accepted modes.

## Heating schedule widget

On a dashboard, add the **Heating schedule** widget of the integration and
choose a heating circuit. It shows:

- the program the circuit runs now, and its setpoint, live;
- the ViCare weekly schedule, one row a day, and the program that runs
  outside the slots (usually reduced);
- the heating curve: slope and shift.

The widget costs no API call: it uses the values of the regular refresh.

The schedule is read-only: change it in the ViCare app. The **Heating curve**
button opens a form to change the slope and the shift (Gladys 5.2 or later;
on Gladys 5.1 the button says so). The curve sets the supply temperature from
the outside temperature:

- too cold when it freezes outside, fine in mid-season: raise the slope;
- too cold (or too warm) whatever the weather: raise (or lower) the shift.

Change it in small steps (0.1 for the slope, 1 for the shift) and wait a few
days between two changes: a building reacts slowly. The room and outside
temperatures kept in the Gladys history help judging the result.

## Gladys 5.2 thermostat (schedule and widget)

Gladys 5.2 can program a heating circuit with its own weekly schedule and show
it in its thermostat widget:

1. In **Integrations → Thermostat**, create an **external** thermostat.
2. Setpoint: the **Target temperature** of the circuit. Mode: its **Mode**.
   State: its **Operating state**. Temperature: its **Room temperature** when
   the circuit has a room sensor, otherwise any room sensor.
3. Attach a schedule if Gladys should program the circuit.

Good to know:

- The setpoint Gladys writes changes the temperature of the program the
  circuit runs in ViCare (normal, reduced, comfort). If the ViCare schedule
  keeps switching between normal and reduced, the setpoints of Gladys land in
  both programs. To let the Gladys schedule rule, set the ViCare schedule of
  the circuit to a single "normal" slot over the whole day in the ViCare app.
  To keep the ViCare schedule, do not attach a Gladys schedule.
- Stopping the thermostat sets the circuit to hot water only: hot water keeps
  being produced. Gladys then also writes its frost protection setpoint, and
  writes the right setpoint back when the thermostat starts again.
- Each value Gladys writes is one API call (an unchanged value is not sent
  again).

## Refresh and quota

- The integration reads every value of a gateway in **a single call**. The
  default interval (120 s) uses about 720 of the 1450 daily calls. With
  several gateways, the interval is multiplied by their number to stay within
  the quota.
- After a command, the new value shows up right away, and the appliance is
  read again about fifteen seconds later to confirm it.
- When the quota is exhausted, the integration pauses until it renews. The
  Configuration screen shows when it resumes (UTC). Raise the refresh interval
  if it happens.

## Known limitations

- Thermostat **presets** (comfort, eco, away) are not offered: Gladys only has
  them since 5.2, and the integration still supports Gladys 5.1.
- When the circuit runs a program without an adjustable temperature (standby,
  frost protection), the target temperature is not shown and cannot be
  changed.
- Not supported yet: burner modulation (Gladys has no matching category),
  solar thermal, photovoltaics and batteries, ventilation, Zigbee thermostats
  and sensors, the temperature of each program, and changing the schedules
  (shown read-only in the widget).
- The clock of the boiler cannot be set from Gladys: the ViCare API has no
  command for it. Set it from the boiler menu.
- Control only goes through the Viessmann cloud: an Internet connection is
  required.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Enter the client ID…", or Connect fails**: paste the Client ID of the
  developer portal and save the configuration **before** clicking Connect.
- **Redirect error while connecting**: the redirect URI of the client on the
  portal must be exactly the one shown under the Connect button.
- **"The ViCare authorization expired or was revoked"**: click **Connect**
  again. Changing the client ID also requires connecting again.
- **"ViCare API daily quota reached"**: wait for the time shown and raise the
  refresh interval.
- **A gateway is offline**: its devices keep their last values, the others
  keep being updated.
- The integration logs detail every error. They never contain your tokens.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que Viessmann ViCare te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before you start | `section` | No | 1. Sign in to the Viessmann developer portal with your ViCare account and create a client whose redirect URI is the address shown under the Connect button below. 2. Paste its client ID in the field below. 3. Save the configuration. 4. Only then, click Connect and sign in with your ViCare account. The Documentation link details every step. |
| Client ID | `string` | Sí | Client ID of the application created on the Viessmann developer portal. |
| ViCare account | `oauth2` | No | Save the configuration with the client ID before clicking Connect: Connect uses the saved client ID, not the one being typed. |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | Seconds between two readings of a gateway. The free ViCare plan allows 1450 calls a day: 120 s uses about half of it, and the interval is multiplied by the number of gateways. |

## Cómo instalar Viessmann ViCare en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: Viessmann ViCare aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/bertrandda/gladys-viessmann:1.1.0`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/bertrandda/gladys-viessmann](https://github.com/bertrandda/gladys-viessmann).

Viessmann ViCare requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

Viessmann ViCare es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [bertrandda](https://github.com/bertrandda), no el equipo principal de Gladys.

- [Explorar todas las integraciones](/es/docs/integrations/), nativas y de la comunidad
